source.method: 30 unique RapidDesign case pages, dynamic media extracted via browser, mid/late video frames sampled with ffmpeg

core_principle: Generate competition-grade PPT pages by choosing a page-specific visual motif first, then arranging only the essential conclusion and evidence around it. Do not produce generic card grids, generic horizontal flowchains, or isolated chart containers.

one_three_ten_second_rule.one_second: The viewer can identify the single dominant visual object or spatial scene.
one_three_ten_second_rule.three_seconds: The viewer can understand the page's main conclusion without reading body paragraphs.
one_three_ten_second_rule.ten_seconds: The viewer can inspect 2-4 supporting evidence points and understand why the conclusion is credible.

global_directives: Each page must define visual_motif before layout: object, scene, map, path, ring, tower, dashboard, product, person, city, mountain, sea, stage, device, certificate, or evidence wall.
The motif must occupy meaningful area, usually 35-70% of the body region, unless the page is a dense evidence/dashboard page.
Use fewer but stronger elements: one main visual, one conclusion, two to four evidence points.
Move detailed explanations to speaker_notes_json. Page text should be conclusion and labels, not full narration.
Maintain deck unity through color, material, title grammar, line language, footer rhythm, and recurring motif fragments, not through repeating identical card layouts.
When using charts, integrate them into a scene: map overlay, dashboard wall, circular system, journey path, evidence strip, or stage panel.
negative_directives: Do not use more than three same-sized white rounded cards as the primary composition.
Do not use a horizontal node-chain flow by default.
Do not wrap every diagram in a big pale empty container.
Do not use evaluation/score wording on competition project pages unless the content itself is about evaluation.
Do not write generic phrases such as 覆盖评分点, 方案完整, 效果显著 without concrete scene evidence.
Do not let the SVG/diagram be the whole design; the diagram should become part of a designed scene.

cover.composition: Full-bleed scene or generated hero image, large project name, subtitle, minimal metadata.
cover.prompt: Design a PPT cover like a premium keynote poster. Choose one domain-specific hero scene or object as the dominant visual. Use the project name as the main typographic event. Do not use cards or web landing-page sections.

contents.composition: Scenic strip or route/map with 4-5 section numbers; current section highlighted by size/color/position.
contents.prompt: Create a directory page, not a meeting agenda. Use a landscape/path/map metaphor and 4-5 numbered chapters. Make the active chapter visually dominant.

architecture.composition: Choose ring, tower, layered pyramid, control room, map deployment, or challenge-capability-solution stage based on content.
architecture.prompt: Convert the architecture into a designed spatial system. Avoid equal card rows. Show hierarchy, flow, dependencies, and output value through scale and position.

process.composition: Road, tunnel, rail, light path, river, or slope with milestones attached to the path and a clear destination.
process.prompt: Design the process as a journey with a visible destination. Milestones should grow along a path, not sit as isolated boxes.

data.intent: Make one result impossible to miss
data.composition: One dominant number/result plus contextual evidence, using badges, map labels, dashboard panels, or chart embedded in scene.
data.prompt: Lead with one result. Use secondary data as proof around it. Avoid four equal KPI cards.

evidence_chain.composition: Claim first, then evidence from source record, process trace, result metric, or scene photo.
evidence_chain.prompt: Show what has been proven and why. Use three evidence anchors with concrete labels. Do not use evaluator-facing score language.

value.composition: Poster-like conclusion with symbolic visual and 2-3 outcome proofs.
value.prompt: Make the page feel like a summary poster. One sentence conclusion, one strong visual symbol, two or three proof points.

market_or_region.composition: Layered map: macro location, target region, route/connection, opportunity badges.
market_or_region.prompt: Use map storytelling. Reveal where, why it matters, and what opportunity exists through spatial layers.

product_or_scene.composition: Product/device/field scene as hero, labels attached to physical parts or usage steps.
product_or_scene.prompt: Anchor the message in a real object or usage scene. Attach capability labels to the object, not to detached cards.

visual_variation_directives: If the previous page used cards, this page must use map/ring/path/tower/stage/photo-overlay instead.
If the page has 4+ items, choose a spatial metaphor rather than a grid.
If the content is abstract, force a concrete metaphor: road for process, ring for ecosystem, tower for hierarchy, map for region, dashboard for operations, certificate wall for proof.
At least one page in every 5-page span should be a scene-led page with image or generated bitmap visual.
Every diagram-heavy page must state why its diagram form fits the content.

audit_rules.blank_or_empty: Fail when body region has large empty area with no intentional focal object.
audit_rules.card_grid: Fail when primary body contains 4+ same-size cards and no stronger focal object.
audit_rules.unclear_focus: Fail when no element is visually dominant by size, color, contrast, or position.
audit_rules.text_heavy: Fail when body paragraphs explain more than labels and short evidence.
audit_rules.diagram_container: Fail when a diagram sits in a large generic container without scene integration.
audit_rules.same_as_previous: Fail when layout differs from adjacent pages only by text replacement.

speaker_notes_policy.page: Keep only headline, main conclusion, labels, key numbers, and short proof phrases.
speaker_notes_policy.json: Put detailed explanation, transition script, data interpretation, and caveats into speaker_notes_json.
